How the paradigms work (animated)

Source: vignettes/articles/concepts.Rmd
concepts.Rmd

Five short animations, one per idea behind the integration paradigms. Each is a small vector graphic, so it stays crisp at any size. The colours follow the package palette: teal and amber for two sources, navy for the result.

Direct integration

The sources are concatenated into one wide matrix and clustered once. Fast and transparent (ADC, ADEC).

Similarity fusion

Each source gives an object-by-object similarity network. The networks reinforce each other through cross-diffusion and converge to one fused network (SNF).

Voting consensus

Many partitions vote on whether each pair of objects belongs together. The votes accumulate into a consensus that is then clustered (M_ABC, CEC, EvidenceAccumulation).

Hierarchy

Per-source hierarchies are consensed into a single dendrogram. The tree is read from the leaves upward to the root (HierarchicalEnsembleClustering, EHC).

Data nuggets

A large set of observations is compressed into a few weighted representatives (nuggets). Feature weights and clustering then run on the small set, which is why the scheme scales to large samples.

Each animation loops. For the full method details, see the method comparison and the guides.
